recovery_analysis.thesis: Sobha closed FY25 with record AED 30bn presales (+30% YoY) and a multi-billion backlog backing its $530m Jul-28 Sukuk, though rating agencies remain watchful of aggressive land-bank capex and shareholder dividend distributions amid regional macro sentiment. Structural recovery anchored by UAE real estate asset perimeter and SOBHA 8.75% Jul 2028 Sukuk seniority.

annotations.topic: H126 Balance Sheet (AED 3.65bn Net Debt, 0.3x D/E)
annotations.note: H126 rev AED 6.6bn, gross debt AED 9.7bn, cash AED 6.1bn, net debt AED 3.65bn (0.3x net debt/equity).
FY25 presales hit AED 30bn (+30% YoY); $530m Jul-28 Sukuk ($300m + $230m tap) monitored for land/dividend outflows.
Moody's affirmed Ba3 CFR and upgraded senior unsecured sukuk to Ba2 Stable; S&P maintained BB but revised outlook to Negative in 2026 on term-loan leverage expansion.

Cash balances include project escrow accounts protected under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007. Disbursements require independent engineer certification against construction progress, insulating project assets from corporate creditors.
Off-plan revenue recognized strictly under IFRS 15 percentage-of-completion. Massive contracted backlog provides 2.5-3.5 years of forward revenue coverage.
Land bank held at historical acquisition cost; revalued market appraisal provides substantial asset cushion (>3.0x net debt).

verdict.stance: Neutral / High-Growth Dubai Developer with S&P Negative Outlook Split (Ba2/BB Neg)
verdict.summary: Sobha closed FY25 with record AED 30bn presales (+30% YoY) and a multi-billion backlog backing its $530m Jul-28 Sukuk, though rating agencies remain watchful of aggressive land-bank capex and shareholder dividend distributions amid regional macro sentiment.

positives: Moody's upgraded senior unsecured sukuk to Ba2 Stable (CFR Ba3) on robust Dubai sales scale (AED 27.6bn prior-year bookings).
Backward-integrated design & construction model protects EBITDA margins and handover quality.
Strong escrow cash collections across Sobha Hartland II and Siniya Island developments.
negatives: S&P revised 'BB' rating outlook to Negative in 2026 due to higher-than-expected leverage from new term-loan facilities & aggressive land/project expansion.
Geographic concentration in Dubai real estate cycle.
Significant ongoing construction capex & working capital commitments.
